China Adds Extra Havana-Beijing Flight as Cuba Fuel Crisis Strands Travelers

By Reuters
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:45
Instaread
Key Takeaways
  • China adds replacement flight CA590 for Air China flight CA866 to fly passengers from Havana to Beijing.
  • Cuba faces an acute fuel shortage, causing airlines to suspend services and leaving travelers stranded amid reinforced U.S. sanctions.
  • The Chinese embassy confirmed the added flight but did not mention the fuel crisis, China's foreign ministry and Air China gave no immediate comment.

China has arranged an additional flight from Havana to Beijing for passengers unable to leave Cuba, as a deepening fuel crisis forces international airlines to suspend services or adjust operations because of refueling difficulties.

The Chinese embassy in Cuba said on Monday that a replacement flight, CA590, had been added for Air China flight CA866 from Havana to Beijing.

The embassy said in a statement that CA866’s schedule had changed frequently in recent weeks due to “technical reasons,” with some flights canceled. It did not refer to Cuba’s fuel crisis.

Flight CA590 was scheduled to depart Havana at 2230 local time on October 19, the embassy said.

Data from Umetrip, a popular Chinese flight information app, showed that CA589, the preceding flight for CA590, had arrived in Havana. CA590 had not departed Havana, according to the app’s records.

The additional flight comes as Cuba grapples with an acute fuel shortage amid mounting U.S. pressure on its government, including a nine-month de facto fuel blockade and reinforced sanctions that have contributed to an unprecedented economic crisis on the island.

The shortage has disrupted transport and aviation operations, leaving some travelers stranded as airlines face difficulties securing fuel for departures from Cuba.

China’s foreign ministry referred Reuters to other government departments when asked for comment. China’s aviation regulator and Air China did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
